Vanessa — thanks for flagging and for the draft redline. Quick legal read and suggested plan below. High level: we can offer a defend & control commitment in limited form for third-party copyright/patent claims that are directly tied to outputs generated by a specific model invocation, subject to notice/cooperation and certain carve-outs. Key points:

1) Proposed pragmatic position (short):
- Redwood will defend and indemnify the Customer for "Covered IP Claims" (third-party claims alleging that the Customer's use of the Service as delivered by Redwood infringes a third party's patents, copyrights, or trademarks), provided that the Customer: (a) gives prompt written notice; (b) permits Redwood to assume the defense and control of the claim; and (c) cooperates in good faith.

2) Critical carve-outs and limitations we should insist on:
- No defense for claims arising from (i) Customer-provided prompts/promoted training data; (ii) Customer modifications to outputs; (iii) Customer's use of the output beyond the documented API behavior; (iv) known third-party open-source code exceptions (list to be specified).
- Redwood reserves the right to select counsel and settle (subject to consent if settlement imposes non-monetary obligations on Customer).
- Monetary cap tied to order form fees (suggest 12 months' ARR or negotiated cap).

3) Evidence & timeline ask to include in acknowledgement (practical):
- Please provide: (i) claimant name and contact details; (ii) precise excerpts of the alleged infringing output and the corresponding model prompts or call IDs; (iii) any third-party registration/copyright documentation; (iv) copies of demand letters and invoicing.
- Proposed dates: Redwood will acknowledge within 48 hours; customer provides evidence within 7 business days; Redwood provides initial position within 10 business days of receipt of complete evidence.

4) Insurance / escrow / hold-harmless commercial asks:
- Ask customer to require Redwood to maintain commercial general liability or technology E&O with $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate (we may negotiate down). Alternatively, propose escrow/retention buckets for claims over a threshold.

5) Suggested customer-facing acknowledgement (one paragraph) ready to send:

"Vanessa — Thanks for notifying us. We take these matters seriously. Please provide the claimant's contact details, the exact outputs at issue, and any demand documents; we will acknowledge within 48 hours of receipt, review the materials, and provide an initial position within 10 business days of receiving complete evidence. Pending review, Redwood is prepared to discuss a limited defend-and-indemnify commitment for covered third-party IP claims subject to the MSA's notice/cooperation requirements and specified carve-outs."

6) Next steps for Sales:
- Send the acknowledgement to EconServ today.
- Simultaneously open a legal matter in our matter-tracker and request the claim file and call IDs from infra (for logs).
- If EconServ asks for broader defend & control, route to CRO for commercial trade-offs (credits or cap increases).

I can draft the two short candidate clauses (defend & control text + indemnity-only fallback) for the customer reply — will attach in a follow-up 60–90 min. If Sales needs to be more conciliatory up-front, I can soften the carve-outs.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Rebecca — thanks for the notice and for sending the materials. We've opened the matter internally and want to confirm next steps so we can move fast:

1) Evidence request (please deliver within 7 business days):
   - claimant name and contact;
   - specific example outputs and the associated call IDs / timestamps / prompts (or the portion of the dataset producing the output);
   - any registration/ownership docs and the original demand letter;
   - copies of any customer-facing materials said to contain the allegedly infringing content.

2) Timeline and initial position:
   - Redwood will acknowledge receipt within 48 hours.
   - Once we receive the complete evidence package, we will provide an initial legal position and proposed path (defend & control vs. indemnity-only) within 10 business days.

3) Initial commercial view:
   - Redwood is prepared to discuss a limited "defend and indemnify" commitment for clearly covered third-party IP claims that arise solely from outputs generated by specific API calls, subject to notice/cooperation and our standard carve-outs (prompt-modified outputs, customer alterations, open-source exceptions).
   - If EconServ requires broader coverage today, please indicate that so we can escalate for commercial approval (insurance/limit/cap trade-offs).

4) Technical contact for logs & call IDs: please share a primary contact who can coordinate with our infra team.

Attachments: none in this reply (we have the PDF you provided).

We appreciate the prompt heads-up. We'll circulate formal candidate language and the redline options to you as soon as legal posts them (target: today + follow-up in 90 minutes).

Best regards,
